literal: Wei Shou, styled Bowei, childhood name Fozhu, a man of Xiaquyang in Julu.
idiomatic: Biography of Wei Shou. Wei Shou, styled Bowei, childhood name Fozhu, was from Xiaquyang in Julu commandery.

literal: Great-grandfather Ji, grandfather Shao.
idiomatic: His great-grandfather was Ji; his grandfather was Shao.

literal: Father Zijian, styled Jingzhong, posthumously granted Pillar of the State and Governor of Dingzhou.
idiomatic: His father Wei Zijian, styled Jingzhong, was posthumously made pillar of the state and governor of Dingzhou.

literal: Shou at age fifteen could already compose in writing.
idiomatic: At fifteen Shou could already write compositions.

literal: When he followed his father to the frontier, he delighted in practicing mounted archery, wishing to distinguish himself through martial skill.
idiomatic: When he followed his father to the frontier, he took to riding and archery, hoping to make his name by martial arts.

literal: Zheng Bo of Xingyang teased him, saying: "Young Wei, how much do you play with halberds?
idiomatic: Zheng Bo of Xingyang jested, "Young Wei, how fond are you of waving halberds?

literal: " Shou was ashamed and thereupon bent his will to study books.
idiomatic: " Ashamed, Shou bent his will to books.

literal: In summer months he sat on a plank bed, chanting along with the tree shade; year after year the plank bed was worn sharp by it, yet his energy did not slacken.
idiomatic: In summer he sat on a plank bed and chanted as he moved with the shade; over the years the bed wore thin at the edges, yet his vigor never flagged.

literal: He became renowned through literary brilliance.
idiomatic: He won fame through literary brilliance.

literal: At first he was appointed Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
idiomatic: His first appointment was erudite of the imperial academy.

literal: When Erzhu Rong wantonly killed court gentlemen at Heyin, Shou was also within the encirclement; because the day was late he was spared.
idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong massacred court officials at Heyin, Shou was caught in the roundup but was spared as dusk fell.

literal: Li Shenjun, Minister of Personnel, valued Shou's talent and learning and memorialized to appoint him staff member of the Grand Secretariat.
idiomatic: Li Shenjun of the ministry of personnel prized Shou's talent and had him made staff secretary in the grand secretariat.

literal: In the third year of Yong'an he was made Northern Master of Guests Lang.
idiomatic: In the third year of Yong'an he was made northern master of guests lang.

literal: When Emperor Jiemin was enthroned, he finely selected close attendants and ordered Shou tested by composing a "Fengshan Shu"; Shou put brush to paper and finished at once, setting down no draft; the text ran to nearly a thousand words, and few places were altered.
idiomatic: When Emperor Jiemin took the throne, he culled his inner circle and ordered Shou to draft a Feng and Shan memorial; Shou wrote it at a stroke without notes, nearly a thousand words with scarcely a revision.

literal: At the time Yellow Gate Gentleman Jia Sitong stood in attendance, deeply marveling, and reported to the emperor: "Though one had talent for seven paces, one could not surpass this.
idiomatic: Yellow gate gentleman Jia Sitong, standing by, was deeply struck and told the emperor, "Even the seven-pace talent could not outdo this.

literal: " He was transferred to Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry; soon he was ordered to take charge of the Daily Record, and also to compile the national history, concurrently Secretariat Attendant; he was then twenty-six.
idiomatic: " He was made gentleman attendant of the scattered cavalry, soon ordered to keep the daily record and compile the national history, with concurrent secretariat attendant; he was twenty-six.

literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign, he again ordered Shou to take up his former duties.
idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaowu of Wei's reign Shou was again ordered to resume his former posts.

literal: Literary edicts piled up; every matter met with approval.
idiomatic: Drafts piled high and every piece pleased the throne.

literal: Yellow Gate Gentleman Cui Juan followed Gao Huan of Qi into court and scorched the age; Shou at first did not visit his gate.
idiomatic: Yellow gate gentleman Cui Juan came to court with Gao Huan and blazed in influence, but Shou at first would not call on him.

literal: Juan drafted the enthronement amnesty for the emperor, saying "We have entrusted Our person to Emperor Xiaowen"; Shou mocked its bluntness.
idiomatic: Juan wrote the enthronement amnesty with the phrase "Our body is entrusted to Emperor Xiaowen"; Shou laughed at its bluntness.

literal: Regular Attendant Li Shen told him of it; Juan bore deep resentment and jealousy.
idiomatic: Regular attendant Li Shen reported this, and Juan came to resent and fear him deeply.

literal: At that time Emperor Jiemin died; Shou was ordered to draft the edict.
idiomatic: When Emperor Jiemin died, Shou was ordered to draft the edict of mourning.

literal: Juan thereupon proclaimed: "In the Putai era Shou went in and out of curtains and canopies; in a single day he composed an edict, finely wrought in phrasing—then all the men of the righteous standard become rebels;
idiomatic: Juan publicly declared, "In the Putai years Shou moved in the inner curtains; he composed an edict in a day with polished wording—by that logic every man who raised the righteous standard is a rebel;

literal: further, Shou's father was aged; he ought to resign office and return to serve; the Southern Terrace was about to impeach him; he was spared only when Minister Xin Xiong spoke for him to commandant of the guard Qi Juan.
idiomatic: Shou's father is old and ought to leave office to tend him; the southern terrace was set to impeach him until minister Xin Xiong pleaded with commandant Qi Juan, and the matter was dropped.

literal: Shou had a younger brother Zhongtong by a lesser mother, who had not been entered in the household register; in fear because of this he recorded him on the register and sent him home to support and serve.
idiomatic: Shou had a younger half-brother Zhongtong, not yet on the family register; terrified by the scandal, he registered him and sent him home to care for their father.

literal: Emperor Xiaowu once mustered troops on a great scale and hunted south of Song and Shao for sixteen days.
idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu once raised a great host and hunted south of Mount Song for sixteen days.

literal: The weather was cold; court and commonalty lamented in complaint.
idiomatic: The weather was bitter; court and people groaned in complaint.

literal: The emperor with his attendants and various consorts displayed strange arts and extraordinary ornaments, mostly outside ritual measure.
idiomatic: The emperor, his attendants, and the palace women showed exotic tricks and outrageous dress, mostly beyond propriety.

literal: Shou wished to speak yet feared; wished to be silent yet could not stop, and so submitted "Nan Shou Fu" to admonish by indirection; he was then twenty-seven—though the words were lush and ornate, in the end they returned to elegance and rectitude.
idiomatic: Shou wished to remonstrate yet feared to; wished to hold silence yet could not, and submitted the "Fu on the Southern Hunt" as subtle counsel; he was twenty-seven—though the diction ran rich and ornate, the piece ended in sober propriety.

literal: The emperor personally wrote an edict in reply, greatly praising it.
idiomatic: The emperor answered in his own hand with high praise.

literal: Zheng Bo said to him: "Had you not met this old fellow, you would still be chasing rabbits."
idiomatic: Zheng Bo told him, "Had you not met me, you would still be chasing rabbits."

literal: At first Gao Huan firmly declined the post of Grand General of the Pillar of Heaven; the Wei emperor ordered Shou to draft the edict, letting him have what he requested.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan first firmly declined grand general of the pillar of heaven, the Wei emperor had Shou draft the edict granting his request.

literal: He wished to add the title Chancellor of State and asked about rank and grade; Shou answered according to fact, and the emperor then stopped.
idiomatic: When the throne wished to make him chancellor of state and asked about rank and precedence, Shou answered plainly and the emperor dropped the matter.

literal: Shou, having not yet gauged the intentions of sovereign and minister, was uneasy because of the earlier affair and sought release; an edict permitted it.
idiomatic: Unable to read sovereign and minister, uneasy over past trouble, Shou asked to resign and was allowed.

literal: After a long time he was made Retainer of the Eastern Headquarters for the emperor's brother's son, Prince Zan of Guangping; Shou dared not decline and composed "Ting Zhu Fu" to convey his mind.
idiomatic: Long afterward he was made eastern headquarters retainer to Prince Zan of Guangping, the emperor's brother's son; Shou dared not refuse and wrote the "Fu on Bamboo in the Court" to set out his feelings.

literal: Soon he was concurrently Secretariat Drafter, and with Wen Zisheng of Jiyin and Xing Shao of Hejian shared equal renown—the age called them the Three Talents.
idiomatic: Soon he was concurrent secretariat drafter, ranked with Wen Zisheng of Jiyin and Xing Shao of Hejian; contemporaries called them the Three Talents.

literal: At the time Emperor Xiaowu was suspicious and wary of Gao Huan; within there were rifts; Shou thereupon pleaded illness and firmly declined, being relieved.
idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu then suspected Gao Huan and rifts opened within; Shou pleaded illness and secured release.

literal: His uncle Cui Xiaofen wondered and asked him; Shou said: "I fear there will be armor from Jinyang.
idiomatic: His uncle Cui Xiaofen, puzzled, asked why; Shou said, "I fear armor will march from Jinyang.

literal: " Soon after Gao Huan marched south and the emperor entered Guanxi to the west.
idiomatic: " Soon Gao Huan marched south while the emperor fled west into the passes.

literal: Shou was concurrently Regular Attendant of the Unimpeded and Upright Scattered Cavalry, assisting Wang Xin on a mission to Liang; Xin was elegant in manner and eloquent in letters, Shou rich and unbound in phrasing—the Liang ruler and all his ministers alike added respect and wonder.
idiomatic: Shou served as concurrent regular attendant for imperial missions and assisted Wang Xin on an embassy to Liang; Xin was elegant and quick in debate, Shou lush in ornament—the Liang ruler and his court all honored them.

literal: Earlier when north and south first made peace, Li Xie and Lu Yuanming were first to carry missions; the talent and bearing of both were alike held in weight by the neighboring state.
idiomatic: When north and south first made peace, Li Xie and Lu Yuanming had led the embassies; both men's gifts were prized by the rival court.

literal: Coming to this, the Liang ruler said: "Lu and Li were men of an age; Wang and Wei revive the moment—who knows what those who come after will be like?
idiomatic: Now the Liang ruler said, "Lu and Li belonged to a destined age; Wang and Wei revive the age—who knows what envoys will follow?

literal: " Shou in the lodge then sold Wu slave-girls to enter the lodge; among his subordinates were those who sold slave-girls, and Shou also summoned and took them, running riot in debauchery; Liang's hostel officers all were punished because of it.
idiomatic: " In the embassy lodge Shou trafficked in Wu slave-girls; when his men did the same he joined them, debauching at will, and every Liang hostel officer involved was punished.

literal: People praised his talent yet despised his conduct.
idiomatic: Men praised his talent but scorned his morals.

literal: On the road he composed "Pin You Fu"; the diction was very beautiful and ample.
idiomatic: On the journey he wrote the "Fu on the Embassy Journey," the diction splendid.

literal: When the mission returned, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Gao Longzhi sought southern goods from Xin and Shou; they could not satisfy his wish, and he thereupon prompted Commandant of the Censors Gao Zhongmi to detain Xin and Shou at his bureau; after a long while they were released.
idiomatic: On their return, vice director Gao Longzhi pressed Xin and Shou for southern luxuries; thwarted, he prompted censor commandant Gao Zhongmi to hold them at the censorate until they were freed long afterward.

literal: When Sun Qian died, Sima Ziru recommended Shou; he was summoned to Jinyang and made Chief Clerk of the Inner and Outer Government Office.
idiomatic: After Sun Qian died, Sima Ziru recommended Shou; summoned to Jinyang, he was made chief clerk of the inner and outer government office.

literal: For receiving orders in violation and opposition he was repeatedly blamed and reproved, and moreover beaten with the rod; for long he did not realize his ambitions.
idiomatic: His orders often missed the mark; he was blamed and beaten and for long found no favor.

literal: It happened that Sima Ziru went on mission to the hegemonic court; Shou borrowed his surplus light.
idiomatic: When Sima Ziru went on mission to the hegemonic court, Shou borrowed reflected glory.

literal: Ziru at a banquet in jest said to Gao Huan: "Wei Shou was the Son of Heaven's Secretariat lang—a great talent of the state; I wish the Great King would lend him a favorable countenance.
idiomatic: At a banquet Ziru jested to Gao Huan, "Wei Shou was the Son of Heaven's secretariat lang—a state talent; I ask the Great King to show him a kind face.

literal: " From this he was transferred to a post in the government office, yet not greatly honored in courtesy.
idiomatic: " By that he became a staff officer in the office, though not yet with full courtesy.

literal: Shou's paternal uncle by the female line Ji Jing had talent and learning, his successive offices famed, all ahead of Shou—yet Shou often slighted and overlooked him.
idiomatic: His cousin Ji Jing was learned and had risen through famous posts ahead of Shou, yet Shou often slighted him.

literal: When Ji Jing and Shou first went to Bing, there was Li Shu of Dunqiu, son of the former Grand Minister of Agriculture Xie, famed for florid eloquence, who once told Shou: "The hegemonic court already has two Weis.
idiomatic: When Ji Jing and Shou first reached Bing, Li Shu of Dunqiu—son of the former grand minister of agriculture Xie, famed for florid debate—once told Shou, "The hegemonic court already has two Weis.

literal: Shou bluntly said: "If you compare me to my uncle by the female line, that is like Yesu compared to you.
idiomatic: Shou blurted, "If you liken me to my cousin, that's Yesu compared with you.

literal: Yesu was son of the former Director of the Masters of Writing, Duke Jibo of Chenliu, famous for dull-wittedness; he delighted in going himself into markets and shops, buying goods at high prices—the merchants together mocked and toyed with him.
idiomatic: Yesu was son of the former director of the masters of writing, Duke Jibo of Chenliu, notorious for stupidity; he loved to walk the markets and pay high prices, a jest to every trader.

literal: Shou slighted Ji Jing, and so compared him thus—his lack of deference was often like this.
idiomatic: Shou despised Ji Jing and matched him so—his insolence was often of this sort.

literal: Shou originally relied on literary talent and surely hoped to stand out and be known; office not being attained, he sought to compile the national history.
idiomatic: Counting on literary talent he had hoped to shine and be noticed; when rank failed him, he asked to compile the national history.

literal: Cui Jin spoke for him to Gao Cheng: "The matter of national history is weighty; your house's father and son hegemonic achievements all must be fully recorded—without Shou it cannot be done.
idiomatic: Cui Jin told Gao Cheng, "National history is grave; your house's hegemonic deeds, father and son, must all be set down—only Shou can do it.

literal: " Gao Cheng memorialized Shou as Concurrent Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, compiling national history.
idiomatic: " Gao Cheng had Shou made concurrent regular attendant of the scattered cavalry to compile the history.

literal: In the second year of Wuding he was made Regular Attendant and concurrently led Secretariat Attendant, still compiling history.
idiomatic: In the second year of Wuding he was made regular attendant, leading as concurrent secretariat attendant, still editing history.

literal: The Wei emperor feasted the hundred officials and asked why the day was called "Human Day"; none could know.
idiomatic: The Wei emperor feasted his officers and asked why the day was called Human Day; none could answer.

literal: Shou replied: "Jin Discussion Officer Dong Xun's 'Answers on Questions of Rites and Customs' says: "The first day of the first month is the cock, the second the dog, the third the pig, the fourth the sheep, the fifth the ox, the sixth the horse, the seventh is human.
idiomatic: Shou answered, "Dong Xun's Answers on Rites and Customs says, "On the first day of the first month is the cock, the second the dog, the third the pig, the fourth the sheep, the fifth the ox, the sixth the horse, the seventh is mankind.

literal: " At the time Xing Shao was also at the side, deeply ashamed.
idiomatic: " Xing Shao, standing by, was deeply mortified.

literal: From the time Wei and Liang were at peace, whenever letters went down to paper it would at once say: "We trust that within your realm it is tranquil; within this realm all lands are at peace.
idiomatic: Since Wei and Liang made peace, every letter opened, "We trust your realm is tranquil; here the empire is at peace.

literal: " Later Liang envoys in their letters then used the word "that" realm, while for themselves still wrote "this"—wishing to show the meaning of having no outside.
idiomatic: " Later Liang envoys wrote "that realm" yet still called their own "this," to show they admitted no outsider.

literal: Shou fixed reply letters to say: "We trust within the realm it is clear and calm; now the ten thousand states are at peace.
idiomatic: Shou fixed replies to read, "We trust the realm is clear and calm; now the ten thousand states are at peace.

literal: " Liang men in replying letters took this as the model.
idiomatic: " Liang envoys thereafter followed that form.

literal: Later when Gao Huan entered court, Emperor Jing invested him as Chancellor of State; he firmly declined and ordered Shou to draft the memorial.
idiomatic: Later Gao Huan came to court; Emperor Jing invested him chancellor of state; he declined, and Shou was ordered to draft the memorial.

literal: When the memorial was finished and presented, Gao Cheng was then attending at the side; Gao Huan pointed at Shou and said: "This man ought again to be a Cui Guang.
idiomatic: When the memorial was done, Gao Cheng stood by; Gao Huan pointed at Shou and said, "This man will be another Cui Guang.

literal: " In the fourth year Gao Huan feasted at the Shrine of Ximen Bao and said to Sima Ziru: "Wei Shou is history officer and writes our good and evil; I hear that during the northern campaign the great nobles often fed the history officers food and drink—did the Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Sima ever feed them or not?
idiomatic: " In the fourth year Gao Huan feasted at the shrine of Ximen Bao and asked Sima Ziru, "Wei Shou as historiographer will write our good and evil—I hear nobles fed the historiographers on the northern campaign; did you, vice director Sima, ever feed them?

literal: Thereupon together they laughed greatly.
idiomatic: They laughed together.

literal: He then said to Shou: "Do not see Yuankang and others hurrying before my eyes and suppose I think it labor—my later-life person and name are in your hands; do not suppose I do not know."
idiomatic: He told Shou, "Do not see Yuankang and the rest scurrying before me and think I mistake it for diligence—my name in later ages is in your hands; do not think I do not know."

literal: Soon he was further made Concurrent Master of Composition.
idiomatic: Soon he was made concurrent master of composition.

literal: Shou long ago in Luoyang was exceedingly frivolous; people nicknamed him saying "Wei Shou startles the butterflies.
idiomatic: In Luoyang Shou had been utterly rakish; men nicknamed him "Wei Shou, startler of butterflies."

literal: Gao Cheng once toured Eastern Hill and ordered Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Yuan and others to banquet.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng once toured Eastern Hill and had attendant gentleman of the yellow gate Yuan and others hold a banquet.

literal: Gao Cheng said: "Wei Shou relies on talent and is unfit for propriety—his shortcomings must be brought out.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng said, "Wei Shou is insufferably proud—his faults must be aired.

literal: Back and forth several rounds, Shou suddenly cried aloud: "Yang Zunyian's reasoning is bent and already fallen.
idiomatic: After several rounds Shou suddenly shouted, "Yang Zunyian's argument is broken and down.

literal: Yin at ease said: "I am broadly with surplus leisure, stand like a mountain unmoved; if I met the one on the road, I fear I would lightly flutter and pass away.
idiomatic: Yang Yin calmly said, "I still have ample leisure and stand unmoved as a mountain; meet the one on the road and I fear I would flutter away.

literal: "The one on the road" is Wei; "lightly flutter" is the butterfly.
idiomatic: "The one on the road" meant Wei; "flutter away" meant butterflies.

literal: Gao Cheng had known it beforehand and laughed greatly, praising it as good.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng had seen it coming and laughed with praise.

literal: Gao Cheng also said: "The words just now are still subtle; you should further point and revile.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng said, "That was still too mild—press harder.

literal: Yin answered at the sound: "Wei Shou in Bing composed a poem; when he had read it before the assembly he finished, saying: 'Beat out from my uncle Ji Jing six hundred hu of rice—you cannot tell this either.'
idiomatic: Yang Yin answered at once, "Wei Shou in Bing wrote a poem and read it before the crowd: 'Beat my cousin Ji Jing for six hundred hu of rice—you cannot tell this either.'

literal: This is known far and near—I do not dare speak falsely.
idiomatic: Everyone near and far knows it—I do not speak idle scandal.

literal: " Gao Cheng delightedly said: "I too heard of it beforehand.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng said with delight, "I heard it too.

literal: " The assembly all laughed.
idiomatic: " The company laughed.

literal: Shou though he spoke to clear himself, no longer resisted, and for life was ill because of it.
idiomatic: Though Shou defended himself, he could not answer back and bore the wound for life.

literal: Hou Jing rebelled and entered Liang, raiding the southern frontier; Gao Cheng was then in Jinyang and ordered Shou to draft more than fifty sheets of proclamation; in not a full day they were finished.
idiomatic: Hou Jing defected to Liang and raided the south; Gao Cheng in Jinyang ordered more than fifty proclamations from Shou, finished within days.

literal: Again he proclaimed to the Liang court, ordering them to send Hou Jing; at the start of night he took up the brush, and by the third watch it was done—the text exceeded seven sheets.
idiomatic: He also drafted a summons to Liang to surrender Hou Jing—brush in hand at first night, done by the third watch, seven sheets and more.

literal: Gao Cheng was pleased with it.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng was pleased.

literal: The Wei emperor once in late autumn held the great archery rite, universally ordering poems composed; at the end of Shou's poem it said: "A letter a foot long summons Jiankang; a folded note calls Chang'an.
idiomatic: The Wei emperor once held the autumn great archery and ordered poems; Shou's ended, "A foot-long letter summons Jiankang; a folded note calls Chang'an.

literal: " Gao Cheng exalted it, turning to the crowd and saying: "In court today there is Wei Shou—he is the state's luster.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng exclaimed and told the assembly, "With Wei Shou in court today the state has its splendor.

literal: Elegant and common, brush and ink, penetrating and running freely—I too have Zicai and Zisheng sometimes compose, but as for phrasing and tone, none reach him.
idiomatic: High and low, ink and polish, all run through his hand—I set Xing Shao and Wen Zisheng to write at times, yet neither matches his tone.

literal: I sometimes harbor a thought in mind, forget and do not speak, speak but do not exhaust it, or a thought has something not yet reached—when Shou presents drafts all are thorough; this too is hard to have.
idiomatic: Sometimes I harbor a thought, forget to speak it, speak but fall short—Shou's drafts fill every gap; that too is rare.

literal: " He was further ordered concurrently Master of Guests Lang, receiving Liang envoys Xie Yan and Xu Ling.
idiomatic: He was also made concurrent master of guests lang to receive Liang envoys Xie Yan and Xu Ling.

literal: When Hou Jing had already overthrown Liang, Prince Fan of Poyang of Liang was then Governor of Hezhou; Gao Cheng ordered Shou to instruct him by letter.
idiomatic: After Hou Jing overran Liang, Prince Fan of Poyang held Hezhou; Gao Cheng had Shou persuade him by letter.

literal: Fan received the letter and forthwith led his troops westward; Governor Cui Shengnian entered and seized his city.
idiomatic: Fan received the letter and marched west with his men; governor Cui Shengnian took the city.

literal: Gao Cheng said to Shou: "Now in settling one province you had a share in the effort; I still regret that 'a letter a foot long summons Jiankang' has not yet taken effect."
idiomatic: Gao Cheng told Shou, "You helped secure a province today, yet I still regret that your line about summoning Jiankang has not come true."

literal: In the second year an edict ordered him to compile the History of Wei.
idiomatic: In the second year the throne ordered him to compile the History of Wei.

literal: In the fourth year he was made Wei Intendant; therefore he was favored with salary and strength, devoted solely to the history hall, unaware of commandery affairs.
idiomatic: In the fourth year he was made Wei intendant, favored with stipend so he could dwell in the history office and ignore commandery business.

literal: At first the emperor ordered the hundred ministers each to speak their intent; Shou said: "Your subject wishes to obtain the straight brush at Eastern Watch and soon complete the 'Book of Wei.'
idiomatic: Once the emperor asked each minister his wish; Shou said, "Your servant seeks the straight brush at Eastern Watch and an early completion of the Book of Wei."
